name: Tāhunanui Beach
bio: A huge, shallow sandy beach on the edge of the city, popular for swimming, kite-surfing and sunsets.

name: Centre of New Zealand
bio: A hilltop marker said to be the geographic centre of the country, with views across the city and Tasman Bay.

name: World of WearableArt and Classic Cars Museum
bio: Extravagant wearable-art garments from the famous WOW show, alongside a gleaming collection of classic cars.

name: Christ Church Cathedral
bio: A grey marble cathedral atop Church Hill at the head of the main street, reached by a broad flight of steps.

name: Suter Art Gallery
bio: One of New Zealand's oldest public galleries, beside Queens Gardens, with strong regional and Māori collections.

name: Abel Tasman Coast Track
bio: A Great Walk weaving through coastal forest between golden beaches, walkable as a day section or over five days.

name: Split Apple Rock
bio: A giant granite boulder split cleanly in two, sitting in the shallows off a sandy cove.

name: Kaiteriteri
bio: A golden-sand resort beach and the main departure point for water taxis and kayak trips into the park.

name: Anchorage Bay
bio: A sweeping golden bay on the Coast Track, a popular drop-off with short walks to Te Pukatea Bay.

name: Cleopatra's Pool
bio: A clear forest rock pool with a natural moss-lined waterslide, a short detour off the Coast Track.

name: Tonga Island Marine Reserve
bio: A protected stretch of sea where kayakers paddle alongside fur seal pups and dolphins.

name: Totaranui
bio: A long, golden beach at the northern end of the park, with a large campground behind the dunes.

name: Te Waikoropupū Springs
bio: Sacred springs with some of the clearest fresh water ever measured, welling up in shades of blue and green.

name: Wharariki Beach
bio: A windswept beach of dunes, caves and the iconic Archway Islands, with seal pups in its rock pools.

name: Farewell Spit
bio: A 30 km arc of sand dunes reaching into the sea, a bird sanctuary visited by guided 4WD tours.

name: Labyrinth Rocks
bio: A maze of narrow passages between weathered limestone outcrops, with little toys hidden in the crevices.

name: Takaka
bio: Golden Bay's laid-back main town of cafés, galleries and markets, and the base for the springs and beaches around it.

name: Lake Rotoiti
bio: A glacial lake whose Kerr Bay jetty, framed by forested mountains, is one of the South Island's best-loved views.

name: Mount Robert
bio: A loop climbing Pinchgut Track to an alpine ridge with views straight down onto Lake Rotoiti.

name: Lake Rotoroa
bio: The quieter, wilder sister lake, reached by a side road through beech forest, with mountains rising from its head.

name: Heaphy Track
bio: The longest Great Walk, crossing Kahurangi National Park's tussock downs to nīkau-lined West Coast beaches.

name: Ōpārara Basin
bio: Huge limestone arches, caves and moss-draped forest on short walks from the end of the Karamea road.

name: Karamea
bio: A remote end-of-the-road town and the gateway to the Ōpārara Basin and the Heaphy Track.
